glosses: A container, typically made of glass or plastic and having a tapered neck, used primarily for holding liquids.

examples.text: Beer is often sold in bottles.

examples.text: I only drank a bottle of beer.

glosses: A container with a rubber nipple used for giving liquids to infants, a baby bottle.

examples.text: The baby wants a bottle.
With Marvin getting older ... and walking now ... I thought it was time to start weaning him off of his bottle.

examples.text: This plant bottles vast quantities of spring water every day.

examples.text: Because of complications she can't breast feed her baby and so she bottles him.

glosses: To refrain from doing (something) at the last moment because of a sudden loss of courage.

examples.text: The rider bottled the big jump.

glosses: To throw away a leading position.

examples.text: Arsenal bottled the Premier League.

glosses: To strike (someone) with a bottle.

glosses: Of pages printed several on a sheet: to rotate slightly when the sheet is folded two or more times.

examples.text: Closely related to creep is the process of bottling. As you may have noticed from your folded sheet of paper, pages don't merely creep when they're folded — they also rotate slightly. This rotation or bottling is caused by the thickness or bulk of the paper.
